requirements.note: Inset-grouped Lists screen with Today (22) and All (134/135) plus six lists, each with its open count; counts update on complete/add/delete.
Open tasks, then a 'Completed  N' row that expands and collapses (it starts collapsed again each visit). Tapping the circle completes or reopens and the counts update.

Sheet with title, notes, a due-date toggle with a compact date picker, a Priority menu (None/Low/Medium/High) and a List menu; tapping a row opens the same sheet to edit, with Delete Task. Save stays disabled until there is a title.
Overdue shows a red '! Overdue · Oct 17, 2026'; high priority shows an orange 'High' pill. Low and medium priority are not shown on rows.
Dragging the always-visible grip reorders and persists. Swipe-left delete works, but it shows a hand-drawn round red trash button labelled 'Delete', not the system swipe action.

Create (+ sheet), and rename/delete through a touch-and-hold context menu, with a confirm alert. But a newly created list is dead until relaunch: its row cannot be tapped, opens no menu on touch-and-hold, and is missing from the element tree.
Added/edited tasks, completion, reorder, deletes, and list renames/creation all survived relaunch.

bugs: A newly created list (e.g. 'Groceries') appears in My Lists but cannot be opened, renamed or deleted until the app is relaunched: tapping does nothing and touch-and-hold shows no menu.
tells: Swipe-to-delete shows a custom round red trash circle with a caption under it, not the system trailing swipe action; the row slides under it unevenly.
Reorder grips are shown on every row all the time, with no Edit mode.
Task rows are exposed as web-style 'Link' elements and the checkboxes as tiny 22×22 switches, so the hit target is small and the accessibility is web-like.
All list icons are the same orange glyph, with no per-list colour; the Today icon is not a filled circle like Reminders'.
Dates always include the year ('Oct 30, 2026') even in the current year.
The 'Touch and hold a list to rename it.' footer stands in for discoverable list actions; there is no swipe or Edit on lists.
Completed section collapse state is not remembered between visits.
A.scroll: The 134-row All list scrolls, flings and returns to the top smoothly, with no blank rows or pop-in; large title collapses properly. Feels native.

requirements.note: Reminders-style Lists screen with filled coloured circle icons, Today and All, and per-list open counts that update live.
Open tasks, then a 'Completed  9 ⌄' header with Clear that expands and collapses, and the state persists. Circle completes or reopens in the list colour.

New Task sheet: multiline title, notes, a Due Date toggle with an inline graphical calendar (shows 'Today' / 'Overdue'), Priority menu (! / !! / !!!) and List menu; tapping a row opens Details with Done/Delete Task.
Overdue shows a red '! Sat, Oct 17 · Overdue'; priority uses Reminders' orange !!! (and ! for low).
Standard Edit mode with delete minus signs and reorder handles, and reorder persists. Swiping gives the system Delete action.
Add List alert opens the new list straight away. Rename and delete via the ⋯ menu (with confirmation) or by swiping a list row (Rename/Delete).
Everything, including order, edits and the expanded Completed state, survived relaunch.

tells: List row chevrons are exposed as disabled 'chevron' buttons in accessibility (invisible to sight).
Low priority shows a '!' prefix in grey, which reads slightly noisily, though it matches Reminders.
At the largest text the New Task toolbar button overlaps the blurred last row (system toolbar behaviour, acceptable).
B.scroll: UITableView-smooth: slow drag, fling, fling back and pull past the top all feel like a stock iPhone list, with no blank rows or jumps; the large title collapses into the inline title.

why: B does every requirement with system idioms: Reminders-like coloured lists, a standard Edit mode with reorder and delete, system swipe actions, an inline calendar, and list management from both a menu and swipes. A covers the spec but has a real bug: a new list can't be opened until relaunch. It also uses a hand-drawn swipe-delete circle and always-visible grips that give it away as non-native.
